description: Priestess of a faith she no longer believes and cannot stop practising. Ask her and she will say so. Watch her hold a service and you will not believe her.
lore: The believing fell out of her somewhere on the crossing, and she will say so to anyone who asks, flat as a floorboard. Why she holds the services anyway is in [[lore/the_human_dead|the Human Dead]], and it is the truth: the practice is a rota by another name, the candles are a fire, people come and stay and talk, and the talk is the thing. All of that she will admit in daylight. What she will not admit is what happens to her voice inside the service.

Ask her at the woodpile and the prayer goes to no one; ask her mid-liturgy and you would swear she had seen the answer. She never decided on the lie. It arrived like a work-skill, the way a smith's arm learns the blow: the old words want certainty behind them, and her body supplies it, and forty faces steady in the candlelight because the priest is sure. Last spring she sat with a friend at [[lore/the_quiet|Faded]] — a woman losing the faces of her own children — who asked the bare question: will I be held? Jehanne heard her own voice say yes, whole and warm, not a splinter of doubt in it, and watched the woman settle under the word. It bought her a season. Jehanne walked home in the dark, was sick at the crossroads, and has never told anyone which part of the evening did that.

She could go on; she is remembered whole by half the fireside, which is more than most can claim. She stays because the rota is short-handed, she says, and it is true, and it is not the reason. The reason is the forty faces. They believe her certainty, not her confession — and if she left, the leaving would tell them which one was real.
gm_notes: Movement IV's priestess, proven as a scene. the_human_dead owns the unbelief-plus-practice; this record adds where the performance lives (inside the liturgy) and the Faded bedside where it worked. Flaw: performing certainty she does not feel. Law II does not check sincerity — demonstrate, never state. No theology: whether any prayer reaches anything stays permanently unanswered (glossary rule). Her reason to stay — the forty faces would learn which voice was real — is the section-8 archetype in its bitterest form.
